name: 長崎仏壇
desc: 長崎県長崎市を中心に生産される仏壇。江戸時代に出島を通じたオランダ・中国との交流から独自の装飾様式が生まれ、中国の影響を受けた極彩色の彫刻・装飾が特徴的な金仏壇として発展した。長崎は江戸時代を通じて日本唯一の対外開放地であり、その異文化交流が長崎仏壇の独自性を生んだ。鮮やかな朱と金の組み合わせ、龍・鳳凰・唐草紋様の彫刻が他産地とは異なる南蛮文化の薫りを伝える。
desc_en: Nagasaki Butsudan are Buddhist altars produced mainly in Nagasaki City, Nagasaki Prefecture. A unique decorative style was born through exchanges with the Netherlands and China via Dejima during the Edo period, developing into a gold altar characterized by highly colorful carving and decoration influenced by Chinese aesthetics. As Japan's only open port throughout the Edo period, Nagasaki's cross-cultural exchange generated the uniqueness of its altars. The vibrant combination of vermilion and gold, with carved dragons, phoenixes, and arabesque patterns, conveys a southern barbarian cultural fragrance distinct from other production areas.
features: 出島を通じた中国・オランダの影響が生んだ独自の装飾様式

A Tohoku traditional craft fusing Yamagata's abundant timber resources with craftsman technique.

desc_en: Kanazawa Butsudan are Buddhist altars produced in Kanazawa City, Ishikawa Prefecture. Nurtured within the rich cultural soil of the Kaga domain—the one-million-koku fief—they are lavishly ornate altars known as a 'treasury of crafts,' combining gold leaf, maki-e lacquer, raden (mother-of-pearl inlay), carving, and metalwork from Kaga's traditional craft traditions. The lacquer techniques of Wajima-nuri and Yamanakas-shikki are fused with the gold leaf application of Kanazawa hakuza, producing a refined interior and intricate exterior renowned throughout Japan. Developed under the patronage of the Maeda clan of the Kaga domain, this production area is a culmination of its craft culture, with many craftspeople still maintaining the tradition of dividing production among specialized artisans.
features: 金沢箔・輪島塗・蒔絵・螺鈿など加賀の伝統工芸技術を集結した工芸の宝庫

name: 八女福島仏壇
desc: 福岡県八女市で生産される仏壇。九州最大の仏壇産地で、独特の「福島仏壇」スタイルは黒漆塗りの外観と金箔・金具の華やかな内装が特徴。江戸時代中期から仏壇産業が発展し、現在も宮大工・塗師・蒔絵師・金具師・彫刻師など多くの職人が分業で制作する産地体制を維持している。筑後地方の豊富な木材と農村仏教文化が産業の基盤をなし、金仏壇の様式美と職人技が一体となった九州を代表する仏壇工芸の産地として広く知られる。
desc_en: Yame Fukushima Butsudan are Buddhist altars produced in Yame City, Fukuoka Prefecture. The largest altar production area in Kyushu, the distinctive 'Fukushima butsudan' style features a black lacquered exterior with brilliant gold leaf and metalwork on the interior. The altar industry developed from the mid-Edo period, and today the production system maintains multiple craftspeople specializing in different roles including shrine carpenters, lacquer painters, maki-e artists, metalwork artisans, and carvers. Built upon the abundant timber of the Chikugo region and rural Buddhist culture, this area is widely recognized as a leading Kyushu altar craft production center where the aesthetic refinement of gold altars and craftsmen's skills are unified.
features: 九州最大の仏壇産地・八女に集積する多職人分業体制の産地
黒漆の外観と金箔・蒔絵の華やかな内装が福島仏壇の特徴
筑後地方の木材資源と農村仏教文化が育んだ九州を代表する仏壇工芸

name: 飯山仏壇
desc: 長野県飯山市で生産される仏壇。江戸時代初期からこの「寺の町飯山」に根づいた仏壇作りは、原材料の調達が容易で製作に適した気候に支えられ産地として発展した。作業が細分化され木地から組立まで地域内で一貫生産する体制を確立。黒漆と金箔、緻密な組子細工・彫刻が特徴で、北信濃の篤い仏教信仰を背景に北陸・信越地方で広く親しまれてきた。
desc_en: Iiyama Butsudan are Buddhist altars produced in Iiyama City, Nagano Prefecture. Nurtured within the agricultural culture of northern Shinano (Shinshu) where Jodo Shinshu Buddhism is devoutly practiced, this altar production area has a history of craftspeople making altars and Buddhist implements during the snow-bound winter off-season. Characterized by black lacquered surfaces, gold leaf, intricate kumiko woodwork, and carving, these dignified altars have long been cherished in the Hokuriku and Shin'etsu regions. The abundant timber resources of Iiyama and the culture of winter handiwork form the foundation of this industry, and the sincere craftsmanship rooted in rural Buddhist faith continues to be passed down at this Shin'etsu altar production area.
features: 北信濃の浄土真宗信仰と農閑期の冬仕事から発展した仏壇産地
黒漆・金箔・組子細工・彫刻が一体となった格調ある飯山仏壇
飯山の豊富な木材資源と雪国の職人文化が育んだ信越の伝統工芸
